key_insight: RSI-Anything turns interaction data into persistent gains by using predictive world models to select actions and update policies only when improvements remain compatible and reliable.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical, domain-general recipe for continuous improvement in systems like code repair, GUI agents, and lab planning without depending solely on expensive external feedback.
method: Use a JEPA-based world model to predict outcomes of candidate actions.
Select learning data and actions based on predicted utility, then adapt the world model conditionally.
Retain updated policy-model pairs only after component and compatibility checks.
evidence_signal: Across multiple benchmarks, the method improved outcomes such as code repair success (26.3% to 31.2%), GUI efficiency (39.4% fewer actions), lab-planning scores (21.80% to 46.01%), and reaction optimization yield (96.15% vs. 82.16%).
watch_item: Because the approach depends on predictive world models, performance may degrade if model drift or environment changes make predictions unreliable.
paper_title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
